question: A perfect cube with a side length of 8 cm has the largest possible sphere fitted inside it. What is the volume of the empty space within the cube?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For the largest sphere inscribed in a cube of side a, the radius is r = a ÷ 2.

Volume of empty space = Volume of cube − Volume of sphere

⇒ Volume = a³ − (4/3) × π × (a/2)³

⇒ Volume = 8³ − (4/3) × π × 4³

⇒ Volume = 512 − 256π/3 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 512 − 256π/3 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• r = 4 cm 
• 
• 
• side a = 8 cm Cross Section of Sphere inside a Cube 

**Given:**

⇒ Side of the cube (a) = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a cube = a³

⇒ Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

**Calculations:**

⇒ The largest sphere inscribed in a cube will have its diameter equal to the edge length of the cube.

⇒ Diameter of the sphere (d) = 8 cm

⇒ Radius of the sphere (r) = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm

⇒ Volume of the cube = 8³ = 512 cm³

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × 4³

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × 64 = 256π/3 cm³

⇒ Empty space volume = Volume of cube − Volume of sphere

⇒ Empty space volume = 512 − 256π/3 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 512 − 256π/3 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Largest Sphere in a Cube

When a sphere is inscribed within a perfect cube, the sphere touches all six inner faces, meaning its diameter equals the side length of the cube (d = a).

Volume Formulas

Volume of Cube = a³ | Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Total Surface Area Formulas

TSA of Cube = 6 × a² | TSA of Sphere = 4 × π × r²

Largest Cube in a Sphere

Conversely, if a cube is inscribed inside a sphere, the body diagonal of the cube acts as the diameter of the sphere (a√3 = 2r).
